question: A 3-week-old newborn is brought to the emergency department by his parents because of 4 episodes of vomiting that occurred that morning. The parents report that the vomit was yellowish-green with no blood in it. The patient was born at 38 weeks' gestation via vaginal delivery and has generally been healthy. He has passed normal stools each day. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears irritable and pale. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 146/min, and blood pressure is 90/55 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft, mildly distended abdomen with no masses or organomegaly. A nasogastric tube is inserted and intravenous fluid resuscitation is initiated. An x-ray shows no gas distal to the duodenum. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "3-week-old newborn presents with vomiting" -> "vomit is yellowish-green" -> "suggests possible intestinal obstruction" -> "x-ray shows no gas distal to the duodenum" -> "indicates possible duodenal atresia or obstruction" -> "need to confirm diagnosis before surgical intervention" -> "upper gastrointestinal contrast series can visualize obstruction" -> 85%

CHAIN: "3-week-old newborn presents with vomiting" -> "vomit is yellowish-green" -> "indicates bilious vomiting" -> "bilious vomiting suggests possible bowel obstruction" -> "x-ray shows no gas distal to the duodenum" -> "indicates significant obstruction" -> "emergent exploratory laparotomy is often required" -> "but need to assess if less invasive options are available" -> "upper gastrointestinal contrast series is less invasive" -> 80%

analysis: The clinical presentation of the 3-week-old newborn, including bilious vomiting (yellowish-green), irritability, pallor, and abdominal distension, along with the x-ray findings of no gas distal to the duodenum, suggests a high likelihood of intestinal obstruction, possibly due to conditions such as duodenal atresia or malrotation with volvulus. In such cases, an emergent exploratory laparotomy is often required to diagnose and treat the underlying cause of the obstruction. Other options, such as an upper gastrointestinal contrast series or abdominal ultrasound, may provide additional information but are not appropriate as immediate next steps given the acute nature of the situation. Therefore, the most appropriate next step in management is an emergent exploratory laparotomy.
